title: Cops Hunt Down 16-Year-Old Mass Shooter
description:
MIDWEST SAFETY: Uncover. Inform. Empower.

Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

MERCH! Midwest-Safety.com

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Tips? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

The shooter who fired first was identified as Christopher Bowie, who was only 16 years old at the time of the incident. The second shooter was identified as a 20-year-old from Tallahassee, but he was not named a suspect, arrested, or charged with a crime in the shooting. Ten people, including Starwide Receiver Tank Dell for the Houston. in Texans, were taken to the hospital with gunshot wounds, mostly to their legs. All victims recovered from their injuries. Christopher Bowie was charged with three counts of attempted second-degree murder while discharging a firearm. Three counts of criminal attempt to solicit or conspire to commit a capital felony, three counts of committing a first-degree felony with a weapon, and one count of possession of a firearm by a minor under the age of 18. He pleaded no contest and was found guilty on all charges. On April 28, 2025, exactly one year after. After the shooting, Bui, who is now 17 years old, was sentenced to 10 years in prison, as well as five years of probation and a requirement to undergo mental health treatment. After his sentencing, Bui filed a notice of appeal. He has since been assigned a public defender, and the state has filed an acknowledgement of the notice. Bui was not involved in the initial fight that broke out, yet he still opened fire into the crowd. Authorities have not established a direct connection between Bui and the individuals involved in the fight, and his specific intent or motive has not been publicly disclosed. Now, this was supposed to be a night of music and having a good time, but as a cop, I've always been baffled how the actions of one or a few people can ruin an entire evening. And this is the tightrope that police walk in these moments because you arrest the suspect but you also have to protect them. And after all the commotion dies down, police are left with the hardest part. controlling the aftermath. But lastly, this wasn't just a shooting. It was a test of everything that officers trained for. Rapid response, crowd control, scene management, and emotional restraint. Because 10 people were shot that night and who knows how much this one incident impacted their lives. But my question is, how do 10 people get shot in a crowded venue and the system only sees one suspect worth prosecuting? I think it's a good question.
